thread:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: paging @Sam @Morgan @Lee — alert: inference-gpu-pool 'prod-infer' queue growth > 95% and HPA not scaling (5m). See alert: https://dash.redwood.example/alerts/8932

Sam: got it, I'm on call. looking at the dashboard now.

Morgan: I'm here too — seeing steady enqueue rate ~1200 rps, tokens/sec up across several models. GPU utilization at 98% for pool 'prod-infer'. HPA target pods unchanged at 8, despite metrics.

Lee: FYI Prometheus scrape latency up, PromAdapter logs show repeated 504s to metrics-api, and metrics-server reports partial list. Could be adapter backpressure.

Sam: opening the runbook: /runbooks/gpu-autoscale.md. First priority: confirm autoscaler metrics pipeline. Morgan — can you tail prom-adapter logs?

Morgan: tailing now. Logs: ```
2026-03-15T12:04:01Z prom-adapter error: upstream timeout while querying /metrics/v1/custom
2026-03-15T12:04:02Z prom-adapter warn: queue size 1200, drop rate 0.12
2026-03-15T12:04:05Z metrics-proxy error: write timeout
```

Sam: that explains it — HPA not seeing custom metrics. Quick mitigation: 1) Scale up dedicated GPU pool to absorb traffic 2) Reroute low-priority tenants to spare pool 3) Restart prom-adapter pod after verifying load. I'll start scale up.

Lee: paging ops to provision additional gpus now (requested +4 gpus, estimated ready in ~6m). Also putting a temporary token-based throttle on non-critical routes via rate-limiter (pmux) so customer-facing apps for enterprise tier still have priority.

Morgan: trying a safe restart of prom-adapter on node cluster-b to unblock metrics. Command: ```kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/prometheus-adapter -l zone=cluster-b``` — will wait 30s for health checks.

IncidentBot: @PagerDuty acknowledged the page.

Sam: monitoring HPA metrics endpoint manually: `curl -s https://metrics-api.internal/custom/infer/gpu | jq .` — result shows stale timestamp 2026-03-15T11:58:00Z, so adapter outage lasted ~6m.

Lee: ops reports new gpus are provisioning (cloud: provisioning-4gpus-req-789). I also opened a temporary autoscale override to bump max pods to 16 so if metrics return, HPA can scale.

Morgan: prom-adapter restarted. New logs: ```
2026-03-15T12:10:22Z prom-adapter info: connection established to metrics-api
2026-03-15T12:10:23Z prom-adapter info: scrapes successful, queue drain started
```

Sam: checking HPA status: `kubectl -n inference get hpa inference-gpu-hpa -o yaml` — now seeing updated metrics and desiredReplicas climbing: 8 -> 14. Good.

Morgan: queue length trending down slowly. Throttle on non-critical routes reduced error rate for enterprise apps. No 5xx for VIP routes after reroute.

Lee: customer impact: some free-tenant inference jobs delayed ~10-30s during peak, we saw ~120 timed-out requests for non-critical routes. I filed a short incident impact note for CS.

Sam: logging live mitigation steps in the incident doc: https://confluence.redwood.example/incidents/1865432109 - include timelines, commands run, dashboards, and owners.

IncidentBot: :white_check_mark: Incident status updated to 'mitigated (partial)' — autoscaling resumed, queue drain in progress.

Morgan: follow-up actions we should capture: 1) Investigate prom-adapter backpressure pattern — maybe increase concurrency or add buffering 2) Add alert for metrics-proxy write timeouts 3) Run a stress test against adapter under synthetic load 4) Validate HPA fallback policy to scale on host metrics if custom metrics unavailable.

Lee: also propose automation: if prom-adapter reports >60s scrape latency, temporarily enable model-serving fallback autoscaler which uses node-level GPU utilization to increase pods.

Sam: agreed. I'll create a backlog ticket and assign to eng-runtime and eng-infra. For now, shifting to on-call handoff. Morgan — can you stay for the 30-minute post-mortem check?

Morgan: yes, I'll stay.

Lee: I'll hand off to the evening on-call in 15m. Key notes in the thread: prom-adapter outage caused HPA blind spot -> HPA didn't scale -> GPUs saturated -> queue growth -> non-critical throttles and temporary scale-up + reroute mitigated.

PagerDuty: Handoff reminder: @NightOnCall assigned. Please acknowledge when you take over.

Sam: adding final checklist: monitor queue < 20, gpu utilization < 85% for 10m, prom-adapter scrape latency < 1s, confirm no regressions in enterprise customer error rate.

NightOnCall: acknowledged, taking over. :thumbsup:

Sam: thanks everyone. I'll follow up with RCA draft and assign action items. :sparkles:
